item.title: Milan church concert strikes a chord for inclusion ahead of Winter Paralympics
item.description: Days ahead of the Winter Paralympics, when disabled athletes will take center stage at the Milan Cortina Games, a choir from northern Italy performed a pop music concert inside Milan’s Sant’Antonio church.

item.title: ‘Flour war’ erupts in Greek seaside town as revelers celebrate the start of Lent
item.description: The Greek seaside town of Galaxidi exploded into a messy and colorful “flour war” on Monday for its annual end of carnival season festivities that mark the start of the Lent season.

item.title: India’s Supreme Court grants temporary relief to tribal Christians in burial dispute
item.description: A three-judge panel of India’s Supreme Court issued a temporary ruling on February 18 restraining the forcible exhumation and relocation of the bodies of tribal Christians from their village burial grounds in Chhattisgarh state.

item.title: On anniversary of Russian invasion, Major Archbishop says Pope Leo understands Ukraine
item.description: The leader of the Catholic Church in the embattled nation says Pope Leo XIV sees the conflict in a “European context.”

item.title: Sri Lanka police arrest former intelligence chief in connection with 2019 bombings
item.description: Police in Sri Lanka arrested the country’s former intelligence chief in connection with suicide bomb attacks in 2019 that killed nearly 270 people and were believed to be inspired by the Islamic State group, a spokesman said.

item.title: Assisted suicide increases rates of non-medical suicide, statistics show
item.description: There were already 12 U.S. states that legalized assisted suicide, and Oregon, the first state to approve assisted suicide, had a dramatic spike in non-medicalized suicide afterwards that peaked at 41 percent.

item.title: Pope Leo will visit 4 African countries as part of his packed 2026 travel plan
item.description: The Vatican on Wednesday announced a busy and lengthy foreign travel schedule for Pope Leo XIV in the first half of 2026, confirming the pontiff will visit Monaco, Spain and four African nations — Algeria, Cameroon, Angola and Equatorial Guinea.

item.title: US immigration law ‘not rooted in hate or xenophobia,’ ambassador says
item.description: In a wide-ranging sit-down interview, new United States Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch addressed several hot-button foreign policy issues, including the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, and the thorny issue of immigration.

item.title: US Ambassador sees potential for ‘Catholic Moment’ with Leo
item.description: United States Ambassador to the Holy See Brian Burch in an exclusive sit-down interview said he sees the potential for a “Catholic Moment” in the U.S. given the high-profile Catholics in the current administration, with history’s first American pope.

item.title: In Lenten meditation, Bishop Erik Varden addresses abuse, corruption
item.description: “Nothing has done the Church more tragic harm, and compromised our witness more, than corruption arisen within our own house” Bishop Erik Varden said to Pope Leo XIV and other Vatican officials on Wednesday..
